newsitem.title: BULGARIA: EBRD REVISES BULGARIA FUNDING DUE TO DELAYED REFORM.
newsitem.headline: EBRD REVISES BULGARIA FUNDING DUE TO DELAYED REFORM.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) revised its funding strategy for Bulgaria after delayed reforms have deterred development of the private sector, the EBRD said on Tuesday.
"The EBRD has approved a revised strategy for Bulgaria which takes into account the critical economic situation in the country," the bank said in statement.
Bulgaria will fail to meet the 60/40 private/public portfolio requirement which is due in June 1997, or five years after the EBRD began operations in the country said the statement.
The bank attributes the unbalanced portfolio to delayed structural reform, a weak and poorly functioning banking system and a slow and reluctant privatisation.
"These adverse conditions are partly due to a lack of corporate governance with local interests and corruption deterring the urgently needed reforms," the statement said.
The EBRD has approved 21 investments totalling 215.5 million European Currency Units in the financial sector, agribusiness, transportation, telecommunications, energy insurance and consumer goods.
Eighteen percent of the signed projects are in the private sector. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
